newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks hit new record after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks hit new record after U.S. data.

text.p: Swiss shares ended more than one percent higher, hitting a record closing high after the U.S. employment cost index report led to a sharp rise in late trade.
Dealers said the first quarter data, which is considered an important indicator of U.S. inflation trends, was favourable for the markets.
Gains in government bond futures and positive corporate news also helped shares.
The blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) ended up 61.8 points, or 1.29 percent, for a a record close of 4,855.1. A new all-time high was reached at 4,864.3 points.
Broad Swiss Performance Index (SPI) rose 33.39 points, or 1.1 percent, to 3,070.95.
Total bourse turnover was 2.23 billion francs.
Dealers said shares were also lifted by U.S. durable goods data and U.S. consumer confidence data, both of which were weaker than expected.
UBS bearer shares topped the active list, rocketing 33 francs, or 2.44 percent, to 1,386. Dealers explained the rise with several buy recommendation due to technical factors and fundamental reasons.
The other two major banks, SBC and CS Group were also more than one percent firmer.
Among insurers, Zurich soared 10.5 francs to 475 ahead of 1996 results which are expected on Wednesday after bourse close. Swiss Re and Winterthur also gained ground.

Novartis registered shares rose 21 francs to 1,914. Roche certificates climbed 180 francs to 12,355. Clariant, whose first-quarter sales rise of 11 percent in local currencies was better than expected, firmed 13 francs to 843.
